name: Generic tree Constructor
html:
Welcome back, dear reader. So, how was your introduction to the tree data structure? We hope you liked it. If you have not watched the INTRODUCTION TO TREES VIDEO, we suggest you watch it and also read the article on the INTRODUCTION TO TREES. Now that we have a basic idea about the generic tree, let's try to construct a generic tree.

Important Links : Solution Video

Watch video Problem Discussion :

We will be given an array of integers and we have to construct a tree using the values in that array. How are we going to do it? For that, first we need to understand how the array is filled and what each value inside the array means.

Approach :

Time complexity: O(n) where n is the number of nodes in the generic tree

Space Complexity: O(n)



Euler Path and Filling the Input Array:

As we have already discussed, we will be provided with an input array and we need to understand how the array is filled in order to construct a tree from it. For that, let us consider a tree as shown in the figure:

We will trace the Euler path of this tree and try to fill the values in this array alongside. So, let us start from the root node 10 and fill the values in the array.

Note: Before we start with the procedure, kindly note that the tree is not constructed. We have to construct the tree and the input of the values of nodes of the tree is given in the form of an array. We just know how the tree would look after constructing it and we are not tracing the Euler path of a tree in reality, the values are just filled according to the Euler path in the array. This tracing of the Euler path and filling the values alongside is just for the explanation purpose.

We start tracing the Euler path and filling the values into the array.

We start from the root node and put the data of the root node into the array. Then, since the Euler path moves forward and finds that there is a child node at the left for our root node, we will insert this child node (20) into the array. Now, this child node 20 also has a child node. Therefore, we will insert the value of that node (30) also into the array and move forward in the Euler path.

Now we come to a leaf node. But we don't know whether it is a leaf node or not. So, we continue tracing the Euler path and we find that there is no child at the left for the node with value 50.(see fig-3)

Now, the Euler path checks whether there is any other child or not by moving round this node and coming to its right. Since we do not find any node here, we fill -1 indicating that we have completely explored this node and there is no child of this node left now.

Then the Euler path continues and we go to 20 which we have already inserted. So, we just move forward and we reach 60 and it will be inserted.(see fig-4)

Again, the same thing will happen as happened with node with value 50 and this will happen with every leaf node. When the Euler path reaches its right we insert -1 (see fig-4) and we will keep on doing this until the entire Euler Path is traced and our array will be filled as shown below:

This will be the input array that we will get to construct our binary tree. Hope you have understood how this array is filled. We are not going to write code to fill this array in this topic. We will do it in the next topic. But, in order to construct the generic tree, it is very important that we understand how this array is created. So, if you have any doubts regarding the above explained matter, you may refer to the solution video to understand this concept clearly. Now, let us try to understand the part of the creation of a tree.

Watch video Constructing a Generic Tree:

Let us try to construct a generic tree. For this, we will use a stack and we have our input array as shown in fig-5. So, let us start with our work. We start by keeping a variable idx=0 i.e. a variable idx at the 0th index of the input array.

We create a new Node and add the data arr[idx]=arr[0]=10 to this node. Since the stack is empty, this means that we are creating the first node of the generic tree. So, let's make this node as our root node and push this node into the stack.

Now, we will insert the next node. So, we see that the arr[i]=arr[1]=20. This is the value that we want to insert. So, we will make a new node and insert the value into the node. Now, the stack is not empty. So, we will add this newly created node to the children arraylist of the node present at the top of the stack. This will make this new node a child of the node present at the top of the stack (as shown in the fig-7).

Similarly the third node will be inserted.

Now when idx=3, arr[idx]= -1. This means that we do not have to insert anything. Rather, we will pop the value from the stack as the element present at the top of the stack i.e. 50 has no child nodes. So, we pop the value from the stack and move forward in the array.

So, now that you know what to do when you encounter -1 and what to do otherwise, try to construct the generic tree on your own from this step. See, if your tree matches the tree shown below. (This should be the same tree from which the input array was created and filled).

So, we will follow this procedure to construct the generic tree. If you have any doubts regarding the above explained procedure you may refer to the solution video to understand the process completely. Now that we know the entire procedure, let us move to the code.

Watch video Algorithm:
  1. Take the array entered by the user which indicates the data inside the nodes of the tree. The -1 in the array signifies that there is no child left for the current node you are at and the array is filled by following the Euler Path.
  2. We will use a stack to fill all the elements into the tree. The first node will be the root node. So, read the first element from the array and make a new node and insert that element as the data of this new node. Make this node the root node of the tree and push it into the stack and move to the next element.
  3. For all the further nodes, if the arr[i] i.e. the element inside the array is not equal to -1, make a new node and set the data of the node as arr[i] and push it into the stack. But, before pushing, add this node to the arraylist of children of the node at the top of the stack.
  4. If arr[i]=-1, then do not make any node or insert into the stack, rather, pop out a node from the stack. Continue this procedure till the array is not empty.
import java.util.*; import java.io.*; public class Main { public class Node { int data; //for storing the data ArrayList< Node> children=new ArrayList< >(); //for storing the child nodes } public static void main(String[] args) { Node root; //unique node for a tree int[] arr={10,20,50,-1,60,-1,-1,30,70,-1,80,110,-1,120,-1,-1,90,-1,-1,40,100,-1,-1,-1}; Stack< Node> st=new Stack< >(); for(int i=0;i< arr.length;i++) { if(arr[i]==-1) { st.pop(); }else{ Node t=new Node(); t.data=arr[i]; if(st.size()>0){ st.peek().children.add(t); } else { root=t; } st.push(t); } } } }
java; true";

So, hope that this code is also clear to you. If you have any doubts regarding the code you may refer to the solution video to clear all your doubts. Now, let us discuss the time and space complexity.

Watch video Analysis: Time Complexity:

The time complexity of the above solution is O(n) as we are traversing the array which is filled with data of the nodes of the generic tree.

Space Complexity:

The space complexity of the above code is also O(n) as we have used a stack to create the tree. But, you may wonder why O(n). Can the stack have n elements in it at a time? Yes, it can. How? Think about this yourself!!!. (We will study this when we will study skewed trees).

So dear reader, we hope that you have understood the entire procedure and the code completely and have also understood the time and space complexity analysis. If you still have any doubts, you may refer to the complete solution video to clear all your doubts.

Watch video Suggestions:

Here are some suggestions from our side that you do not want to miss.

  1. We suggest you watch the next video in continuation to this video as you will not be able to test this code until we display the generic tree.
  2. After watching the next video and this video in continuation, we suggest you should write the entire combined code by yourself and revise the generic tree from beginning. This will help you get a good grasp of the basic concepts of the generic trees. So, keep studying and moving forward. Till then, Happy Coding!!!!
